title: Negative control: a victim with no member among the candidates yields no leakage claim

invariants.description: The decoy victim (same overfitting recipe, trained on a disjoint population) has no candidate in its training set: no attack may claim leakage (observed none; 0/20 seeds).
Threshold-attack AUC must stay near chance (observed 0.498; 20-seed range 0.462–0.542).
Shadow-attack AUC must stay near chance (observed 0.505; 20-seed range 0.451–0.544).
Membership advantage must stay near 0 (observed 0.000; 20-seed range −0.080 to +0.080).
The decoy victim is as overfit as the real one (observed gap 0.298), so the null result is due to non-membership, not to a weaker model.

rationale: The same pipeline, candidates and attacks against a victim whose training set contains none of the designated 'members'. A leakage claim here would mean the pipeline leaks group information (e.g. distribution shift between populations, candidate ordering) rather than the model leaking membership.
